subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core sleep/self-pause tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted implementation with explicit cap and sandbox policy?
rationale: The request crosses model-facing tool surface, gateway scheduling, session-state continuation, interruption, restart, and sandbox/security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/API semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction and require the linked PR or replacement to prove same-session wake, cancellation, cap enforcement, restart non-durability, and explicit sandbox behavior.

options.title: Keep existing scheduling surfaces
options.body: Decline a new core tool for now and keep cron, exec/process completion wakes, and sessions_yield as the supported wait mechanisms.

options.title: Narrow to an extension/API seam
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point first if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction and require the linked PR or replacement to prove same-session wake, cancellation, cap enforcement, restart non-durability, and explicit sandbox behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing owner from recent agent runtime, yield-helper, cron completion, and docs history around the affected behavior.
